transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-10
Start: 15:00 PDT | Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Ethan (Redwood CSM), Jordan (Vellum Head of ML), Maya (Eng Mgr), Liam (Finance), Sofia (Security)
Links referenced: QBR deck (shared), cost-breakdown sheet (redwood_link/usage.xlsx), SOC2 + security pack (redwood_link/security.pdf)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be partial): Discussed rising per-token cost linked to embedding pipeline growth, two transient outages last month, propose dedicated capacity pilot + private deployment constraints check.

00:00 Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I think we have about 45 minutes on the calendar, we'll run through usage, a couple incidents, and then talk about next steps. Jordan, Maya, you had asked for the economics piece up front so we'll get to that early, ok?
00:22 Jordan: Yep, thanks Alex. We are especially interested in how we can flatten the cost curve for search embeddings — it's spiking.
00:35 Maya: Sorry, quick mute—yeah sorry. And we'll want to understand SLOs if we move more traffic to Dedicated.
00:50 Priya: Quick intro, I'm Priya on the SE side, I'll own the benchmark and the perf data if we run a dedicated pool; I'll also show a couple optimizations we're shipping that might help before committing.
01:10 Liam: Hi, Liam from finance; small ask: can you give us projected savings for 6/12 month reserved? Numbers matter to procurement.
01:22 Alex: Totally, we'll include three tiers in the pricing scenarios — light/medium/heavy commit — and a burst policy. We'll send a modeled tco sheet afterwards.
01:40 Jordan: Also curious about the fallback behavior we saw in March when a regional pool got saturated — we lost a few low-latency endpoints and the UI experienced queuing. Any notes on root cause?
01:55 Priya: I can take that. There were two factors: one was the autoscaler reacting slowly to a sudden spike of long-seq generation, and two was a misconfigured routing rule that prioritized cheaper variants which had longer cold-starts. We're shipping an autoscaler tuning change that'll reduce reaction time; plus we can pin traffic to higher-priority variants during busy windows.
02:30 Sofia: For security, we need to confirm KMS integration and whether audit logs ship to our SIEM. Also data residency — some PHI-adjacent fields must stay in eu-west-1.
02:47 Alex: Good call, we'll surface the Private deployment checklist. Ethan, do you want to say where those docs live?
02:53 Ethan: Yes, I just dropped the security pack and the private-deploy checklist in chat (redwood_link/security.pdf, redwood_link/private-checklist.md). The SOC2 report is there, and we can do an encrypted delivery of artifacts if needed.
03:10 Maya: Quick clarification: if we do dedicated, can we still keep the hosted API for dev and fall back if capacity is maxed?
03:20 Priya: Yes, we support hybrid routing — you can pin production to a dedicated pool and fall back to hosted variants or cross-region. Fallback policies are configurable per-route.
03:40 Jordan: Alright let's look at usage: we've seen embeddings usage jump 3.2x quarter over quarter — mostly from nightly batch indexing — and chat inference is steady but growing at 40% month-over-month. The monthly token spend showed a 28% increase in cost.
04:05 Alex: Did the cost increase align with model changes or sequence length?
04:12 Jordan: Both. We switched to a higher-capacity base model for responses in late Jan, and nightly jobs started including longer prefixes.
04:25 Priya: Two levers: batching and prefix caching. We're releasing smarter KV/prefix caching that will avoid re-computing prefixes across similar prompts; that alone often drops token usage on heavy batch workloads. Also dynamic batching windows can reduce p95 cost but may increase latency slightly.
05:00 Liam: Can you quantify? Even rough numbers help us pitch internally.
05:10 Priya: In internal runs we've seen 15-30% token cost reduction on embedding pipelines with caching, and up to 25% with batching for certain sequence distributions. But your mileage will vary by prompt set; that's why we want to run your dataset through the dedicated benchmark.
05:45 Jordan: We want the benchmark to approximate production: 60% nightly batch embedding, 35% interactive chat, 5% other. Also important: p99 latency under 350ms for chat.
06:05 Priya: Noted. We'll simulate that traffic mix and report p50/p95/p99 plus token cost per 1M tokens.
06:20 Alex: On the reliability incidents: two incidents in March, one was 14 min of degraded tail latency in us-west, another was a 9-min cache warming issue after a rollout. We added more robust rollout canaries and adjusted fallbacks. Any remaining concerns?
06:45 Maya: Do we have a post-mortem for the 14-min incident? I don't remember getting that.
06:50 Ethan: We posted a short incident summary to the support case; I'll attach the fuller post-mortem and the mitigation steps.
07:05 Jordan: For the security checklist — about KMS: we require customer-managed keys (CMKs) in our KMS for decryption at rest, is that supported now?
07:20 Priya: We support external KMS via our private deployment path and for Dedicated we have an integration offer for customer-managed keys via a KMS proxy; full CMK in customer account for on-prem/VPC is supported. We'll map this in the checklist.
07:45 Sofia: Also audit log retention — we need 12 months of request-level logs retained and exportable to our Splunk. Is that doable?
07:55 Alex: Yes, audit logs can be routed to your S3 bucket or exported via our SIEM integration; retention is configurable. We'll confirm the retention SLA and export format in the pack.
08:15 Liam: Back to economics: if we reserve a 6-month commit at medium level, what ballpark savings should we expect vs pure hosted pay-as-you-go?
08:30 Alex: Typical outcomes we see are 20-40% savings depending on utilization and caching effectiveness. We'll model three scenarios and include sensitivity to caching gains.
08:40 Jordan: Procurement will push for a clause to allow us to step down if usage doesn't materialize — is there flexibility on commit terms?
08:50 Alex: Yes, we can discuss step-down windows or graduated commitments; we'll include those in the three-tier proposals.
09:05 Priya: One more technical note: upcoming runtime change will improve KV-cache reuse across similar prompts, but it requires licensable quantization for some model variants — we'll flag which variants will benefit.
09:25 Jordan: Good. On roadmap: we want to align on timelines — can you confirm when the caching and autoscaler changes are GA?
09:35 Priya: Caching improvements are on the rollout schedule for late April (internal rollout week of 2026-04-27) and autoscaler tuning is in the first-half May patch. We'll include dates in the follow-up.
09:55 Maya: Can the caching feature be toggled per-route? We need to test without affecting some latency-sensitive endpoints.
10:05 Priya: Yes, it's opt-in per-route and per-model, with canary controls.
10:20 Jordan: Ok, let's talk pilot. We'd like to run a dedicated pool pilot for 2 weeks with a small reserved commit to measure real savings. Is that feasible?
10:30 Alex: Absolutely. Pilot steps: (1) define traffic mix + dataset, (2) schedule benchmark window (Priya run), (3) analyze results & propose commit levels, (4) if green, roll into 6/12-month commit.
10:50 Liam: Finance needs the modeled TCO by next Thursday to include in our supplier review — that's 2026-04-15.
11:00 Alex: That's doable. Action item for me to send pricing + tco.
11:10 Sofia: For the private deployment gating: we need to confirm network design — VPC peering vs private link, allowed egress ranges, and whether we can airgap certain components.
11:28 Priya: We'll map the private topology options; full airgap requires the on-prem package and a separate control plane, which is doable but has extra lead time.
11:45 Jordan: Any competitors we should be watching? We've seen procurement references to Anthropic and OpenAI as alternatives for hosted and Anthropic for dedicated-style offers.
11:58 Alex: Noted. We'll include a short competitive note in the QBR deck.
12:10 Ethan: I'll schedule the follow-up QBR in two weeks to walk the benchmark results and the pricing sheet.
12:18 Jordan: Sounds good. Thanks.
12:22 Alex: Quick recap — action items and owners in the doc; Priya will kick off the dedicated benchmark, Alex sends pricing/tco by 4/15, Sofia to share compliance list by 4/17. We should reconvene after the benchmark.
12:40 Maya: Thanks everyone.
12:45 End of call (approx 48 min)

Notes on transcript quality: speaker turn-taking is accurate but there are some mis-heard proper nouns; timestamps are approximate. Some phrases were auto-corrected by the transcription engine.
